article.text:
Curation is a high growth early-stage industry.
Two and a half years ago it barely existed as a business. Today roughly $10B sits in curated vaults.
Coinbase and Robinhood now run their earn products on them, and each passed $500M in deposits in September.
More than 30 curators are now active, including established names like Steakhouse Financial, Sentora, Gauntlet, and recent entrants like Galaxy Digital, Bitwise Asset Management and Armitage by Wintermute.
Underneath sit the vaults: the onchain infrastructure curators use to set risk parameters and allocation rules. A year ago we argued that vaults would become the default way to allocate liquidity onchain. That has become the consensus, and institutions are moving into the space.
But a vault has come to mean very different things, depending on the power of its curator. We think of it as a spectrum. On one end are noncustodial vaults, where the curator sets the rules but cannot change allocation without users consent or take control of user assets. On the other end are discretionary vaults, where the operator custody customer assets, and can move assets as they see fit to run more complex strategies.
Despite Morpho Vaults being designed as noncustodial, with the combination of in-kind redemptions, timelocks, role-based access controls and immutable contracts, the same open-source infrastructure could also be forked and configured to create something that looks more like a discretionary vault.
At the end of the day, there is no one size fits all. Different needs will require different vault infrastructure. The more diversity we have at the vault infrastructure layer, the more tools we have to bring all types of credit onchain. We believe the more diverse the vault ecosystem is, the more tools we have to bring all types of credit onchain.

Holding SOL?

Whether you're building a long term position, or you're waiting for your next trade, Jupiter gives you 8 different ways to earn on it:

1. Lending (~4% APY)
Supply SOL into an Earn Vault on Jupiter Lend to earn interest from borrowers.

In return, you'll receive jlWSOL, a receipt token that grows in value over time without the need to claim any rewards.
 
2. Native Staking (~4.8% APY)
Delegate SOL to Jupiter's Validator to start earning staking rewards, while you help secure the network.

Note: Natively staking/unstaking takes up to 2 days. If you want to start earning immediately, look into JupSOL.
 

3. Swap into JupSOL (~5.6% APY)
JupSOL is staked SOL that stays liquid, so you can use it in DeFi.

The underlying staked SOL earns a combination of staking rewards, MEV & priority fees that gives it a higher yield than native staking.

Over time, your JupSOL balance stays the same, while its redemption rate continues to grow.

Then, when you want to make your next trade, simply swap out.
 

4. Earning while you borrow
Borrowing against SOL on Jupiter Lend doesn't mean it has to stop earning.

When you supply JupSOL or SOL as collateral, it continues to earn staking rewards or a Supply APY, respectively.

In addition, Jupiter's Native Staked Vaults unlock a new capability: You can supply natively staked SOL from 5 different validators (Jupiter, Helius, Nansen, Dawn, & p2p) without needing to unstake your position.

Then you can put your borrowed funds to work, keeping in mind that loans accrue interest, and debt can carry with it a liquidation risk.
 
5. Multiply your yield with looping
On Jupiter Lend, Multiply lets you borrow against  your JupSOL and buy more, potentially increasing its yield.

A JupSOL/SOL loop works like this:
1. Supply JupSOL as collateral
2. Borrow SOL against it
3. Swap the borrowed SOL into more JupSOL
4. Redeposit JupSOL

Steps 2-4 repeat in loops until your target leverage is reached, and this looping happens atomically in a single transaction.

When Multiplying, keep tabs on the respective supply and borrow APYs in addition to your position health.
 

6. Earn trading fees via Smart Vaults
Smart Collateral allows a paired position to serve as liquidity inside of Jupiter Lend AMM, adding swap-fee revenue to any supply APY.

With the SOL-JitoSOL smart Vault, you can simply supply SOL and the vault will autocompose the pair for you. 

Then you can borrow against your position and use those funds however you'd like in DeFi.

But do be mindful of the net Supply and Borrow APYs.
 

7. Using Jupiter Offerbook
Jupiter Offerbook provides fixed-rate, fixed-term USDC loans against collateral like SOL.

A lender funds the offer, and you can use the borrowed USDC elsewhere. But you should note: This isn't a yield product for SOL. Rather its a way to obtain liquidity which you can use in DeFi.

Additionally, Offerbook provides a leverage long option where you deposit USDC and pick an asset like SOL to amplify your exposure to its price.

Although this also isn't technically 'earning on your SOL', it allows you to earn on SOL's price appreciation.
 
8. Mint or swap to JLP (Currently ~10% APY)
JLP provides liquidity to Jupiter Perps. In return, 75% of fees generated flow back into the pool, while part of the pool's SOL is natively staked for additional yield.
However, JLP gives you partial SOL exposure through a basket of assets, rather than exposure to SOL alone.
Yield accrues automatically by holding JLP, with nothing to stake or claim.
 
If you’re going to hold anyway, you might as well earn

Lending earns borrower interest, staking earns network rewards, and looping has the potential to earn amplified yield.

You have plenty of options, but if you decide to just hold your SOL, make sure the choice is intentional.

Otherwise, you're leaving easy gains on the table.

article.title: Fixed Rate Multiply: Leveraged Yield with a Defined Cost of Capital
article.preview: Kamino Fixed Rates bring a defined cost of capital and duration to onchain leverage, where financing has historically been dominated by variable-rate, open-term borrowing. This lets borrowers
article.text:
Kamino Fixed Rates bring a defined cost of capital and duration to onchain leverage, where financing has historically been dominated by variable-rate, open-term borrowing. This lets borrowers structure leveraged positions around known funding costs rather than utilization-driven rate changes.
With Fixed Rate Multiply, a user selects an asset and target leverage, and Kamino builds the position in one transaction. The debt comes from a fixed-rate reserve, locking the financing cost for the full term, while Auto Rollover can carry the position into another eligible fixed term at expiry without requiring manual refinancing.
The first Fixed Rate Multiply vault, AUTO/wYLDS, went live on September 21 with Figure and HastraFi. Since launch, the broader AUTO Market has scaled to $35M in fixed-rate loans, while AUTO supply has grown from $9M to $55M.
How Fixed Rate Multiply Works
Fixed Rate Multiply uses Kamino’s existing one-click leverage flow, but the borrow is originated at a fixed rate for a defined term instead of at a variable rate.
A user selects an asset and target leverage, and Kamino builds the position in a single transaction:
A flash loan provides the capital needed to reach the target leverage
The initial deposit and flash-borrowed funds are converted into the collateral asset
The full amount is deposited into Kamino as collateral
The debt asset is borrowed from a fixed-rate reserve and used to repay the flash loan
The result is a leveraged position with a financing cost that is fixed for the full term.
If any step fails, the transaction reverts and no position is created. Closing runs the same flow in reverse. The flash loan fee is 0.001% per transaction.
 
What Does a Fixed Rate Change?
Fixed Rate Multiply gives leveraged strategies a defined cost of capital over a defined period.
Instead of borrowing from a variable-rate reserve, the position borrows from a reserve configured for a specific asset, rate, and term. Once the loan is originated, that rate remains fixed through the end of the term, regardless of changes in utilization elsewhere.
Today, AUTO/wYLDS uses three 30-day wYLDS reserves at 5.30%, 5.75%, and 6%. Each reserve has its own available liquidity, and borrowers access that liquidity directly when opening a Fixed Rate position.
As Kamino expands Fixed Rates across additional terms and markets, these reserves can form the basis of a broader onchain yield curve.
Fixed-term borrowing also introduces different tradeoffs from open-term variable credit. Fixed rates can price at a premium to the prevailing variable rate, and closing during the initial term may incur an Early Repay Penalty to compensate lenders that committed capital for that duration. After the first rollover, positions can be closed without that additional penalty.
AUTO/wYLDS
AUTO is a yield-bearing token, backed by near-prime U.S. auto loans originated by Agora Data, structured through Figure Forge, and minted through HastraFi. The AUTO/wYLDS vault deposits AUTO as collateral, borrows wYLDS at a fixed rate, and loops the borrowed capital back into AUTO, maintaining USD-denominated exposure. Entry and exit route through Figure’s mint and redeem infrastructure rather than relying on secondary-market liquidity.
 
Auto Rollover: Carrying Positions Across Fixed Terms
Fixed-rate credit becomes significantly more useful onchain when borrowers can manage duration without rebuilding positions at every expiry.
Three days before the end date, a position enters its rollover window. If eligible fixed-rate liquidity is available, the loan can move into a new term automatically instead of requiring the borrower to close and manually refinance.
At expiry, Kamino follows the available path in order:
Roll into another eligible fixed term: If qualifying fixed-rate liquidity is available, the position continues into a new term.
Move into the variable-rate reserve where supported: If a fixed-rate rollover is unavailable, the debt can fall back to variable borrowing for the same asset in the same market.
Auto-repay: If neither path is available, the protocol begins repaying the debt from collateral according to the market’s configured Auto-repay mechanics.
 
Auto Rollover gives borrowers the defined cost of capital of fixed-term credit without turning every maturity into a manual refinancing event.
Users can disable rollover from the position interface, and the position lifecycle shows the active term, rollover window and expected expiry path.
Liquidations
A fixed rate removes financing-rate volatility during the active term. It does not remove collateral or liquidation risk.
AUTO/wYLDS has a maximum LTV of 78% and a liquidation LTV of 80%. A position opened near maximum leverage therefore has less room for relative movement between AUTO and wYLDS before reaching the liquidation threshold.
AUTO continues to accrue yield while interest accrues on the wYLDS debt. As long as AUTO’s yield remains above the fixed borrow rate and the relative value of the two assets remains stable, LTV should decline over the term. If that spread reverses or AUTO falls relative to wYLDS, LTV can increase.
Fixed Rate Multiply makes the financing cost predictable, but collateral performance, position sizing and liquidation risk still need to be managed throughout the term.
Defined Cost of Capital with Continuity Across Terms
Fixed Rates introduce a new function to onchain leverage: the ability to finance a position at a known cost for a defined period while maintaining continuity across maturities.
A borrower can calculate the financing spread at entry, size the position against that cost and hold through the term without the borrow rate repricing with utilization. As the term approaches expiry, Auto Rollover can carry the position into another eligible fixed term rather than forcing the borrower to rebuild it manually.
Fixed Rate Multiply packages that infrastructure into the same one-click experience already used for leveraged strategies across Kamino.
AUTO/wYLDS is the first Fixed Rate Multiply vault. From here, Kamino is expanding Fixed Rates across new markets and reserves, while adding new functionality around term selection, rollover and fixed-rate liquidity. As that infrastructure develops, a broader range of strategies will be able to access defined financing directly onchain.

article.preview: Trading on Securitize’s registered broker-dealer platform on Solana and on the upcoming NYSE ATS and OKXICE TSV, Securitize Stocks give eligible investors global access to 1:1-backed U.S. equities
article.text:
Trading on Securitize’s registered broker-dealer platform on Solana and on the upcoming NYSE ATS and OKXICE TSV, Securitize Stocks give eligible investors global access to 1:1-backed U.S. equities with the rights and economic benefits of the underlying shares.
 
 
Today, we’re proud to announce the launch of Securitize Stocks, bringing some of the world’s most widely held U.S. equities onchain for eligible investors in the United States, European Union (EU) and other permitted jurisdictions worldwide.
The initial offering on Securitize will include security entitlements to shares of AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOG, TSLA, META, AMZN, NFLX, CRCL, SPCX, MSTR and PLTR. Securitize Stocks will initially launch on @Solana and trade on Securitize’s registered broker-dealer platform.
Securitize Stocks are also expected to trade on the new 24/7 digital trading venue being developed by the New York Stock Exchange (@NYSE), subject to the venue’s launch and applicable regulatory and operational requirements. The planned connectivity would create another pathway for tokenized U.S. equities to trade through infrastructure being developed by one of the world’s leading exchange operators.
Unlike products that primarily provide economic exposure to a stock’s price, Securitize Stocks are backed 1:1 by underlying shares, structured to preserve the investor rights and economic benefits associated with those shares, and convertible, where available, to direct ownership on the books of the issuer’s transfer agent. The offering is designed to accelerate adoption of issuer-sponsored tokenization as issuers increasingly embrace tokenization.
 
Securitize Stocks give investors:
1:1 backing and security entitlements. Each token is backed one for one by an underlying share and represents a security entitlement under UCC Article 8, preserving applicable rights and economic benefits including dividends and, where the underlying class carries them, voting rights. This sets Securitize Stocks apart from products that are primarily designed to track a stock’s performance.
Global availability. Securitize Stocks will be available to eligible investors in the U.S., EU and other permitted jurisdictions, subject to applicable securities laws, sanctions requirements and other restrictions.
No share lending. Shares backing Securitize Stocks will not be lent out. The tokens are designed to support additional onchain utility over time, including supported lending and collateral markets like Aave.
A bridge to issuer-sponsored tokenization. Securitize Stocks use a convertible entitlement token (CET) structure. When a company adopts issuer-sponsored tokenization, investors can convert their security entitlements into actual shares recorded on the company's register, through Securitize's partnerships with leading transfer agents.
Compatibility with evolving U.S. market structure. The offering is designed to be  consistent with SEC guidance on tokenized securities. Secondary market trading is offered for Securitize Stocks in a regulated manner through its broker-dealer, without the need for exemptions. Securitize Stocks are also expected to be eligible for trading on  Tokenized Securities Venues (TSVs) as contemplated by the SEC’s Innovation Exemption.
 
Securitize Stocks are also expected to be available on the OKXICE Tokenized Securities Venue (TSV), which combines @OKX’s blockchain technology and global reach with the regulatory experience and institutional connectivity of Intercontinental Exchange (@ICE_Markets), parent company of the New York Stock Exchange. The TSV will bring tokenized U.S. equities onchain in a compliant, permissioned environment, with plans to unlock 24/7 trading, instant settlement and self-custody of exchange-listed securities for a global audience.
 
Securitize selected Solana as the launch network for Securitize Stocks onchain trading, with transactions settling in USDC. Solana is also one of the networks where Securitize's own tokenized common stock has traded since its NYSE listing in July.
 
Infrastructure for an Onchain U.S. Equities Market
Securitize Stocks bring together infrastructure spanning blockchain, liquidity, brokerage, clearing, settlement and transfer agency to connect traditional U.S. securities markets with onchain markets.
At launch, Securitize Stocks will be available through Securitize’s existing Solana PropAMM, with @jumptrading, which will serve as a market maker to support liquidity, price discovery and execution consistent with applicable market requirements. Trading will initially be available during extended hours, with plans to move toward 24/7 availability. Securitize Stocks will trade alongside issuer-sponsored tokenized equities including Securitize’s own stock, SECZ. Access will remain subject to onboarding, KYC/AML checks, jurisdictional eligibility and applicable securities laws.
“Bringing U.S. equities onchain requires liquidity infrastructure capable of delivering the execution quality investors expect from modern markets,” said a spokesperson for Jump. “PropAMMs on Solana have demonstrated that onchain markets can deliver tight spreads, deep liquidity and transparent price discovery at significant scale. We’re excited to bring that technology on Securitize’s platform to Securitize Stocks and help build efficient, liquid markets for tokenized U.S. equities.”
Institutional market participants are also expected to play a growing role as tokenized equities develop. @Ripple Prime plans to support the launch of Securitize Stocks and explore opportunities to incorporate the assets into its broader institutional trading ecosystem.
 
Tokenized equities also create the potential for traditional securities to become more useful within onchain financial markets, including through supported lending and collateral applications.
 
Behind the onchain trading experience, Securitize Stocks will connect with established securities-market infrastructure for clearing, custody and settlement.
 
Learn more about Securitize Stocks at stocks.securitize.io.
 
About Securitize
Securitize (NYSE: SECZ), the leading platform for tokenized assets with approximately $5B in AUM as of September 2026, is bringing the world onchain through tokenized funds in partnership with top-tier asset managers such as Apollo, BlackRock, BNY, Hamilton Lane, KKR, VanEck and others. It is the only company operating regulated digital-securities infrastructure in both the U.S. and EU, and has been named to the Forbes 2026 Fintech 50 and CNBC World's Top Fintech Companies 2026 lists.
